_comment: Illustrative default thresholds for DealLens rule engines. They are NOT industry standards; they were chosen as conservative screening levels for a demonstration and should be calibrated per engagement. Each rule documents its rationale.

large_movement_pct.rationale: A >50% period-over-period change in a key line item is unusual enough to confirm with the source.

min_annual_periods.rationale: Three historical periods are commonly requested for trend analysis in due diligence scopes.

revenue_decline_consecutive.rationale: Two consecutive declines suggest a trend rather than a one-off.

gross_margin_deterioration.rationale: A 3 percentage-point fall in gross margin is material for most cost structures.

ebitda_margin_deterioration.rationale: A 3 percentage-point fall in EBITDA margin warrants explanation of cost drivers.

ocf_below_ebitda.rationale: Operating cash flow persistently below 70% of EBITDA may indicate weak earnings quality or working-capital absorption.

receivables_outpacing_revenue.rationale: Receivables growing 15pp faster than revenue may indicate collection issues or revenue timing.

inventory_outpacing_revenue.rationale: Inventory growing 15pp faster than revenue may indicate obsolescence or overstocking.

working_capital_absorption.rationale: An increase in trade working capital above 5% of revenue absorbs significant cash.

high_leverage.rationale: Net debt above 3.5x EBITDA is a common screening level for elevated leverage; covenant levels vary.

negative_fcf.rationale: Negative free cash flow in two or more periods indicates reliance on external funding.

large_unexplained_movement.rationale: Large movements in material line items should be explained by management.

significant_ebitda_adjustments.rationale: Adjustments above 10% of reported EBITDA materially affect the earnings base used in valuation.

customer_concentration.rationale: A single customer above 20% (or top five above 50%) of revenue is a concentration risk.

reported_vs_recalculated.rationale: Reported subtotals differing from recalculation by more than 2% suggest mapping or arithmetic issues.
